appearance.description: One black-on-white projected frame containing rounded filled site marks and numerous thin solid or broken/dashed interior traces. Eight perimeter site marks, eight additional rounded lobes, and one small partially merged site-like dark lobe are visibly locatable. This is an appearance register, not a proven vertex count.
appearance.siteCountConvention: 17 apparent site/lobe locations including the uncertain J lobe; no claim that all are separate vertices or that hidden vertices exist.
appearance.outerRods: Generally thick continuous black strokes. Filled sites obscure the ends at their centers.
appearance.interiorRods: Narrow strokes, mostly broken/dashed, with some continuous sloping fragments. Stroke overlaps and ink fusion must not be interpreted as graph joins.
appearance.labels: No legible site labels, numeric values, directions or legend visible. Minor peripheral ink marks are not treated as sites or relations.

ambiguityLocationTable.exactUnresolvedQuestion: Is J a separate site and which I/J/K/rightward/downward rods actually end there, rather than merge into or pass behind the short J-to-W04 contact?
ambiguityLocationTable.whyPixelsDoNotDecide: Small filled lobe and multiple dark fragments share pixels; the I-J interval and J rim are not separated.

ambiguityLocationTable.exactUnresolvedQuestion: Where does the nearly vertical L-upper chain terminate, and does the K-right/up trace end at L or continue into D/another rod?
ambiguityLocationTable.whyPixelsDoNotDecide: D fill, A-D stroke, D-F stroke, L upper rim and broken segments obscure which contacts belong to which chain.

ambiguityLocationTable.exactUnresolvedQuestion: Which interior traces end on the middle W10 contacts or H, versus cross them or continue behind them?
ambiguityLocationTable.whyPixelsDoNotDecide: The frame stroke and H rim coincide with narrow dashed/solid corridors; there is no independent junction marker at the middle contacts.

ambiguityLocationTable.exactUnresolvedQuestion: Assign every incoming/outgoing connector to O or P and recover any O-P rod and the segmentation of the frame-like diagonal.
ambiguityLocationTable.whyPixelsDoNotDecide: The two rounded lobes overlap and share black fill with the thick diagonal; no exposed O-P interval resolves adjacency. Connected ink does not prove an edge.

ambiguityLocationTable.exactUnresolvedQuestion: Does the shallow O-M corridor actually attach at N, pass behind its rim, or represent separate O-N and N-M rods, and what crosses D-F/H-G?
ambiguityLocationTable.whyPixelsDoNotDecide: N's upper rim hides the relevant segment and nearby frame crossings have no independent site mark.

ambiguityLocationTable.exactUnresolvedQuestion: Pair every segment descending from N with its endpoint; resolve the vertical/diagonal corridor and crossings near (318,270) and frame contact (351,316).
ambiguityLocationTable.whyPixelsDoNotDecide: Broken segments, diagonal crossings and merged frame ink do not show unique endpoint pairings. No new site may be inferred at the bend/crossing.

ambiguityLocationTable.exactUnresolvedQuestion: Locate the lower end of the L-vertical chain and pair the multiple approaching lower diagonals at Q without joining near crossings by assumption.
ambiguityLocationTable.whyPixelsDoNotDecide: Separated dashes terminate near intersecting corridors and Q's filled rim; the hidden pairing is not uniquely exposed.

ambiguityLocationTable.exactUnresolvedQuestion: For contacts (119,63), (284,30) and (344,73), distinguish separate rods ending on frame rods from crossing/continuing chains, and determine whether these unmarked contacts are actual graph vertices.
ambiguityLocationTable.whyPixelsDoNotDecide: Trace-to-frame contact is visible, but there is no separate rounded site or endpoint/junction convention; neither hidden sites nor frame-component transitive connections can supply the missing edges.

ambiguityLocationTable.exactUnresolvedQuestion: Separate the intersection at (140,323) and the two thin traces at bottom-frame contact (157,373); identify which terminate versus continue.
ambiguityLocationTable.whyPixelsDoNotDecide: No site is marked at either contact, and narrow traces meet the thick frame in shared pixels.

ambiguityLocationTable.exactUnresolvedQuestion: Are the shallow middle chain and M-up/right chain separate frame-ending rods or continuations meeting at (407,149)?
ambiguityLocationTable.whyPixelsDoNotDecide: Their contact with the thick rightmost rod is visible but not uniquely typed or separated into source graph endpoints.

ambiguityLocationTable.exactUnresolvedQuestion: Recover the full shallow dashed lower-middle chain leaving the O/P region and its endpoint beyond the D-F crossing.
ambiguityLocationTable.whyPixelsDoNotDecide: Only separated fragments and crossings are visible; a complete endpoint pair cannot be assigned without completing the missing trace.

ambiguityLocationTable.exactUnresolvedQuestion: Are the K-down/left and O/P-left traces two independent frame contacts, a continuing connector, or a joined graph vertex at (30,231)?
ambiguityLocationTable.whyPixelsDoNotDecide: They merge against a thick rod without an independently visible site or endpoint convention.

independentAssessment.basis: Rounded locations and many visible rod contacts are identifiable, but the complete actual graph cannot be reconstructed from the exposed pixels without assuming hidden continuations, unmarked sites or a junction convention. The inventory deliberately records corridor fragments where one-to-one edge pairing is unavailable.
